issues.reason: Cardinality and Quantifiers, generics & scope both state that a definite/grouped plural with a distributive predicate keeps the group event AND adds the per-member (Implication (PartOf $x <group>) ...) rule ("the dogs barked" is the worked example), and none of burned / showed / left / collected / drew is a reciprocal-aggregate predicate or marked "together", so the rule is owed at all five sites.

The compound-kind genus rule is defined only for a modifier_noun "whose last word is a real head noun", `bloomed` is a participial adjective and not a noun, and the instruction set's own warm_blooded example emits no genus, so (Inheritance salt_bloomed bloomed) hands every lantern the property `bloomed` — content the text never states.

"The surface tense decides, mechanically" requires a past copular to wrap its categorical atom, and the copular-with-time-modifier dual-emit is shown as reified state + `(Past (Member alice ill))`, so the bare `(Member $x lit)` conclusion asserts an untensed, still-holding lit state that the past-tense "stayed lit" does not claim.

Thematic roles reserves `Patient` for an object the action creates, destroys, consumes or physically changes; the threads are deposited unchanged by the leaving, and the stated tiebreak ("When the test is unclear, default to Theme") points the same way.

gaps_confirmed: No licensed way to corefer an anaphoric definite mass NP ("The mire-essence", "The mist-light") back to an antecedent stored as a bare kind filler, so the parse mints fresh witnesses and the discourse chain breaks.

Compound ADJECTIVE formation (noun + participial adjective, "salt-bloomed"): Compound concepts covers verb_object, verb_particle and modifier + head-noun only, so no rule states whether a genus atom is licensed — only the warm_blooded example, which emits none.
new_gaps: Non-Gregorian ordinal dating ("day 460 of Year 2", "day 461 of Year 2"): the Time term inventory presumes calendar month/day and CE-year expressions, so (Day 460) reuses the day-of-month slot outside its range and (Year 2) the CE-year slot; a licensed form would need a day-of-year / era-year term that a day-of-month or CE-year query cannot falsely match.

Bare MASS NPs in episodic clauses have no stated treatment: the bare-plural episodic rule mints a group witness and the bare-kind filler is reserved for non-specific objects, but nothing covers a mass noun as an episodic subject ("Mire-essence formed in a cauldron") or as a later-referenced episodic object — which is what leaves one passage holding both `mire_essence` (bare kind) and `sk_mire_essence_1` for the same stuff.
defect_summary: Issue 0: each of the five definite-plural group events (burned, showed, left, collected, drew) must additionally carry its per-member (Implication (PartOf $x <group>) (And ...)) rule at (STV 1.0 0.9) beside the group event, exactly as the parse's own s3_rule and s6_rule already do. Issue 1: `salt_bloomed` must stay an opaque property symbol with no decomposition atom, following the instruction set's warm_blooded precedent. Issue 2: the continuation-copular rule's flat half must be the tense-wrapped (Past (Member $x lit)), matching the (Past (Member $x salt_bloomed)) the same parse emits at s3_rule. Issue 3: the deposited threads take (Theme sk_leave_1 sk_thread_1).
notes: The parse is internally inconsistent rather than uniformly wrong: s3_rule gets the tense-wrapped distributive copular exactly right while s6_rule does not, and s1/s7 correctly keep "together" collective while five unmarked plurals lose their distribution rule. Separately, (CardinalityPhrase sk_nightmoth_1 "handful") records the phrase as "handful" where the instruction set's vague-quantity lexicon lists it as "a handful" — the reviewer raised this only in notes and I have not scored it.
